summary: Mission Control: Lunar Explorer is a browser-based educational game that lets students experience designing and flying a real space mission. Players act as Mission Engineer for an unmanned orbiter sent to find water ice at the Moon’s south pole. They build a spacecraft within a $100M budget, choose a launch vehicle, and pick one of three Earth-to-Moon transfer routes. They then fly a 180-day mission, making decisions when incidents like communication blackouts occur. The game uses real engineering ideas such as the rocket equation, battery energy, and data downlink limits. A final report scores the mission in eight categories. Built on NASA Mission Viz 3D assets, it makes mission trade-offs visible and hands-on for learners.
details:
Mission Control: Lunar Explorer is a browser-based educational game where players design, launch and fly an unmanned orbiter to study water ice at the Moon’s south pole.

How it works: Players pick spacecraft components within a $100M budget, choose a launch vehicle, and select a direct, faster or fuel-efficient Earth-to-Moon transfer. They then run a 180-day mission with live fuel, battery, delta-V and data tracking. Random incidents such as communication blackouts pause the mission and require a decision. A final report scores the mission in eight categories.

Benefits and impact: It makes real mission trade-offs (mass, power, fuel, cost) visible and hands-on for students.

Tools: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, X3DOM/WebGL, NASA Mission Viz 3D assets, hosted on Vercel. 193 automated checks validate the simulation.

SI acknowledgment: Parts of the code for this project were written and debugged with AI assistance from ChatGPT. The project idea, design decisions, game rules and testing were done by the team.
